Figure 1:Can visual generation expand what unified multimodal models know?Left:Images contain rich visual information that accompanying text may leave unspecified.Middle:Knowledge reproduced in generated images is not necessarily accessible through text-only QA.Right:We first supply new facts only through training images and test text-only QA across seven knowledge categories.
Direct transfer is partial; alignment on a subset of entities can improve access on the remaining entities, with interleaved image–text alignment yielding higher average accuracy than textual alignment.
Figure 2:Overview of the text-to-image dataset.Here we show examples from the seven visual knowledge categories. Each panel shows an entity, a training image, and the target attribute value.

Figure 4:Overview of the KTP training and evaluation protocol.(a) Training:All entities receive T2I supervision,
with target attribute values shown in images but omitted from captions.
A subset of entities additionally receives textual or interleaved
image–text alignment supervision.(b) Evaluation:For entities without alignment supervision,
we measure textual accessibility through text-only QA and visual accessibility through image generation.
Figure 6:An example of an entity with visually accessible but textually inaccessible knowledge.
Figure 7:An example of an entity with textually inaccessible knowledge that becomes accessible with visual CoT.
